findings.title: Default tolerance cannot see the surface step the ghost-hover shot targets
findings.route: Proposed fix (concrete fix, needs your confirmation)
findings.scenario: You change the player's icon buttons so hovering no longer lightens them — the surface token goes back to what it was before the full-bleed layout PR. You push, the new web VR job goes green with the ghost-hover shot included, and you merge believing the screenshot proved the hover still works. It did not. At Playwright's default tolerance that surface step is 17 times too faint for even one pixel to be counted as changed.
findings.whats_wrong: The ghost-hover shot's stated job (:227) is to measure a background-token step, and at the default tolerance that step is invisible to the comparator. Measured against the installed comparator: the cutoff is 35215 x 0.2^2 = 1408.6, and the step --elevate over --rail scores 80.7 — 17x under. So reverting hover:bg-elevate to hover:bg-muted, the exact regression the full-bleed layout PR records having shipped, changes ZERO counted pixels and the shot passes. The doc ran this signal-side check for the OTHER new shot (the tooltip, 526 px, "Far past the tolerance") and never for this one, so it is an oversight, not a decision.

before.text:
3. **Playwright's default tolerance is enough** — decided 2026-09-26. Its `threshold` defaults to
   `0.2` in YIQ colour space and `maxDiffPixels` is unset, so a pixel must differ noticeably to
   count and then a _single_ such pixel fails. The worst drift measured here is ±1/255 in one
   channel, about `0.004` — fifty times under that threshold. Going stricter (`threshold: 0`) would
   buy nothing the evidence points at, would make element-clipped shots impossible, and would give
   the repo two comparison policies instead of one. So the shots pass no comparison options at all,
   exactly as `client/` does.
| Ghost hover on the rail   | hover `open-file-button`                             | `hover:bg-elevate` measured against `--rail`          |

**Ghost hover on the rail** — PR #170 finding 10. `client/src/components/ui/Button/Button.tsx` gives
the ghost variant `hover:bg-elevate`, and #170 adds three surfaces it can land on:

```css
--elevate: oklch(93.5% 0.006 240.4deg); /* the raised step a control shows under the pointer */
--rail: #f4f6f9; /* recessed — the left rail */
--panel: #fbfcfe; /* raised — the transport footer */
```

The step is strongest against Storybook's white canvas, which is the only place it is photographed
today, and weakest against `--rail` — where it could regress to invisible with every existing gate
green. `OpenFileControl.tsx` renders `variant="ghost"` on `--rail`, so hovering it is the shot.

regression (the Positioner's `z-index` set back to `auto`) changed **526 pixels** in a 200×100 crop,
the arrow and that band. Far past the tolerance, so the shot catches it — but it is a sliver, not a
missing tooltip.

findings.after:
Two edits, neither reopening the settled default-tolerance decision.

(1) In consequence 3 (:105-108), add the signal-side floor after the noise figure: at threshold 0.2 the comparator's per-pixel cutoff is 35215 x 0.2^2 = 1408.6, so a grey-on-grey step must clear roughly 53/255 of luminance to be counted at all — which puts this repo's surface tokens under it: --elevate against --rail scores 80.7, --muted against --elevate 44.7, and --panel against --background 5.3.

(2) In the ghost-hover row's reason column (:227) and as a Risks bullet, state that the screenshot alone cannot see the surface step, and prescribe asserting the hovered button's computed background-color before the shot — the way the accessibility lane already polls getComputedStyle (web/e2e/a11y.e2e.ts:87, :173) and the way the transport-toggles bullet already prescribes for the tempo percentage.
findings.why_it_works: It closes the hole on the signal side rather than by tightening the comparison, so the settled "Playwright's DEFAULT tolerance, same as client/" decision stands untouched. It also reuses a pattern already live in the same test lane, so the implementer copies rather than invents.
findings.spike:
SPIKED AND CONFIRMED, with the reviewer's arithmetic reproduced independently from the installed playwright-core 1.61.1 and the real tokens in client/src/styles.css. Cutoff 1408.6 exact. Formula is the real 0.5053*dY^2 + 0.299*dI^2 + 0.1957*dQ^2 (coreBundle.js :6865-6904), not the reviewer's shorthand; test is |delta| > maxDelta (:6798); maxDiffPixels falls back to 0 (:7271) so ONE counted pixel fails. Measured: --elevate/--rail 80.7 (17x under), --muted/--elevate 44.7 (31x under), --panel/--background 5.3 (268x under). The oklch->sRGB conversion was validated against three values styles.css asserts in its own comments. Also confirmed the full-bleed layout PR (f98537cd) really shipped hover:bg-muted -> hover:bg-elevate, and --color-elevate maps to the raw token with no alpha (styles.css:110).

TWO REFINEMENTS, BOTH STRENGTHENING IT: the default lives at coreBundle.js:7260 (not :7261, which is the closing brace); and even the case the doc calls strongest (:250, against Storybook's white canvas) scores 244.6 — still 6x under.

ONE LIMIT THE WALK-THROUGH MUST NOT OVERSTATE: the ghost variant also carries hover:text-foreground, and the icon rests at text-muted-foreground (OpenFileControl.tsx:119); that colour change scores 4412.0 and IS counted. So the shot does catch "hover failed entirely". What it cannot catch is a change to the BACKGROUND token — which is exactly what :227 claims it measures. Keep the wording on "cannot see the surface step", never "sees nothing".
findings.verification_reason: Arithmetic independently reproduced from the installed comparator source and the real tokens: cutoff 1408.6 vs 80.7 (17x under) for the step the shot claims to measure, and 44.7 (31x under) for the exact revert that already shipped once as PR #170 commit f98537cd. The doc measured the signal side for the tooltip shot (526 px, :268-269) and never for this one.
findings.contradiction_note: No later section resolves it. The only threshold/tolerance discussion in the whole doc is 102-108 (grepped: "threshold" hits 72,102,105; "tolerance" hits 102,269; "maxDiffPixels" hits 72,103). No signal-side pixel measurement is given for the ghost-hover shot anywhere, unlike the tooltip shot at 268-269.

findings.section: Process changes this carries (670-675), against the CI section (443-445)
findings.title: A guard assertion cannot be repointed at the container job, because its subject is gone
findings.route: Proposed fix (concrete fix, needs your confirmation)
findings.scenario: You implement the gate, move web/'s browser lane into the container, and run the repo's own workflow-guard test. It fails: one assertion demands a browser-install line in ci.yml that your new job deliberately does not have. The spec told you to repoint both broken assertions at the new web job, so you go looking for the line to point at — and there is none. You now invent the replacement yourself, and the quality job that ci-green waits on stays red until you guess right.
findings.whats_wrong: The spec prescribes ONE remedy ("Both must be repointed at the new web job") for two assertions that need two different ones. The browser-install assertion's subject ceases to exist in ci.yml after the move — which the same sentence states one clause earlier — so there is nothing to repoint it at. Guessing wrong either deletes coverage silently or leaves the quality job red with no stated correct target.

before.text:
The new `web` job follows the `vr` job's container recipe, not the `setup-js` composite: `corepack
enable && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`, and no `playwright install` because the
browsers are baked into the image. It carries the same guard every other path-filtered job has —

the one file in this list whose failure you cannot see before pushing. Two assertions break:
  `:40` requires a literal `run: pnpm --filter @notation-hero/web run test:e2e` line, which the
  trimmed `e2e` job no longer has, and `:44` requires a
  `pnpm --filter @notation-hero/web exec playwright install --with-deps chromium` line, which the
  container job deliberately does not need. Both must be repointed at the new `web` job — the test
  case is even named _"the e2e job runs the web Playwright lane, not only the client one"_, which

findings.after: Split the remedy instead of prescribing one for both. Say that the test-invocation assertion is rewritten to match the new job's actual run line (pnpm --filter @notation-hero/web exec playwright test --config=playwright.e2e.config.ts), and that the browser-install assertion is REPLACED by one pinning the new job's container: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble line — since the image pin is what makes "no install needed" true, and nothing else in the test suite pins it.
findings.why_it_works: It gives each broken assertion its own named target, so neither is left to invention, and it preserves the coverage the browser-install assertion existed to provide by moving it onto the thing that now guarantees the same property.
findings.spike:
SPIKED AND CONFIRMED. The browser-install assertion's subject really does cease to exist in ci.yml, and nothing in the repo already pins the container image tag in a test.

ONE WIDENING the finding understates: the test-invocation assertion is not straightforwardly repointable either — the new job's only run line is "exec playwright test --config=..." (doc :454), which does not match "run test:e2e", so it needs its literal rewritten too, not merely repointed. The finding's distinction still holds and is the sharper point (that assertion's subject still exists somewhere to point at; the browser-install one's does not), but the After text must cover both.

LINE REFS TO CORRECT: the browser-install regex spans workflow-guards.test.mjs:42-45 with the literal on :44.
findings.verification_reason: The assertion really is the literal browser-install run line, and the doc's own CI section (:444) says the container job installs no browsers, so "Both must be repointed at the new web job" (:674) is impossible for that one.
findings.contradiction_note: Nothing elsewhere in the doc offers an alternative remedy for :44, and nothing in the repo already pins the container image tag in a test: the only source-file occurrence of `container: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble` is .github/workflows/ci.yml:211 (all other hits are docs), so the finding's proposed substitute assertion does not already exist.

findings.section: CI — web/'s whole browser lane moves into the container (452-455) + A failing run gives you a zip (618-620)
findings.title: The new job's report upload has no stated condition, so a red run uploads nothing
findings.route: Proposed fix (concrete fix, needs your confirmation)
findings.scenario: Your web VR run goes red on a real pixel change. You open the run to download the report and compare the before and after images — and there is no artifact attached. The upload step never ran, because GitHub skips a job's remaining steps once one fails, and the spec never said to guard the upload. Since web/ deliberately gets no hosted diff page, that zip was the only way to see what changed.
findings.whats_wrong: The spec pins the new job down to the exact artifact name and the exact paths, but never states the upload step's if: condition — the one thing that makes the failure path work. An unconditional upload step never runs on exactly the run that needs it. Both sibling uploads in ci.yml already solve this and explain why.

before.text:
```yaml
- name: web browser lane (end-to-end + accessibility + visual regression)
  run: pnpm --filter @notation-hero/web exec playwright test --config=playwright.e2e.config.ts
```

| Job                             | Artifact                       |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `vr` (client Storybook VR)      | `playwright-client-vr-report`  |
| `e2e` (client only, after this) | `playwright-client-e2e-report` |
| `web` (both lanes, one run)     | `playwright-web-report`        |

The `e2e` job's upload also **drops** `web/playwright-report/` and `web/test-results/` from its
`path:` list — those paths belong to the new job now.

So a red `web` VR is read the way any other Playwright failure is: download `playwright-web-report`
from the run's Artifacts and open it with `npx playwright show-report`. Revisit the day that download
becomes a real annoyance — then there is a measured case to size the work against.

findings.after: Spell the upload step out next to the test invocation in the CI section: an actions/upload-artifact step named playwright-web-report, guarded by if: ${{ !cancelled() }} rather than if: failure() — so a flaky-then-passed retry's trace survives, matching the vr job's upload (ci.yml:224) and the e2e job's (:399) — with path: holding the exact web/playwright-report/ and web/test-results/ literals the workflow-guard test pins, plus retention-days: 7 and if-no-files-found: ignore as both siblings use.
findings.why_it_works: It copies a solved pattern from the two sibling jobs in the same file, including the reason the stricter if: failure() is wrong, so the failure path works on the first try and the guard test's pinned path literals keep matching.
findings.spike:
SPIKED AND CONFIRMED. Both sibling uploads carry if: ${{ !cancelled() }} plus a comment explaining why it is not if: failure(), and the spec really pins only the name and paths. The doc's only if: anywhere is the job-level paths-filter guard at :446.

LINE REFS TO CORRECT: the finding cites the siblings' if: as ci.yml:222-223 and :396-398; those ranges are the step name plus the explanatory comment. The if: ${{ !cancelled() }} itself is on :224 and :399. Both siblings also carry retention-days: 7 and if-no-files-found: ignore, which the new job equally needs and the doc equally omits.
findings.verification_reason: Both sibling uploads carry `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` with a comment saying why not `if: failure()`, the spec pins only the new artifact's name and paths, and :618-620 tells the reader to download that artifact on a red run - which an unconditional upload step would never produce.
findings.contradiction_note: Grepped the whole doc for "if:", "upload" and "retention": the only `if:` is the job-level paths-filter guard at :446, and the upload hits (473, 484, 485, 488) all concern artifact NAMES and the e2e job dropping the web paths. No upload step, and therefore no `if:` condition, is prescribed for the new job anywhere.

findings.section: Blocking from day one (508-510), against The pixel-stability measurement (71-80) and the parallelism bullet (572-574)
findings.title: Day-one blocking is warranted by a measurement covering two of the eleven shots
findings.route: Proposed fix (concrete fix, needs your confirmation)
findings.scenario: You read that the measurement "found no flake", so turning the gate on blocking from day one looks safe. Weeks later an unrelated PR goes red on the tracks-popover shot. Nine of the eleven shots never had determinism data — two of them could not, because those popovers do not exist until Plan C ships — and the runs that did pass were taken one worker at a time, while CI runs them in parallel.
findings.whats_wrong: The no-flake claim is cited as the warrant for having no grace period, but its evidence covers /play's default loaded state plus the long-score state: 2 of 11 shots. The doc's own parallelism bullet already concedes the measured shots are "untested in parallel". Because the gate blocks with no grace period, the first flake in one of the nine unmeasured shots surfaces as a red ci-green on somebody's unrelated PR.

before.text:
Sixty runs in `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble`, three shots × twenty runs each, at
`threshold: 0` and `maxDiffPixels: 0` — the harshest comparison Playwright allows, where a single
byte of difference in a single channel fails. The **first** run of each shot writes the baseline and
compares against nothing, so every ratio below is out of the **nineteen comparisons that follow it**:

| Shot                                    | Identical runs |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| Full page (contains the rendered score) | **19 / 19**    |
| Page with the notation masked out       | **19 / 19**    |
| Notation box only (element-clipped)     | 3 / 19         |

**Blocking from day one.** `web` joins `ci-green`'s `needs:` list alongside `a11y`, `vr` and `e2e`.
`client/` VR already blocks, and the measurement found no flake to earn a grace period against: a
visual gate nobody has to obey is one people learn to scroll past.

- **The shots run in parallel, like every other test here — decided 2026-09-26.** The 60-run
  measurement was taken at `--workers=1`, so these particular shots are untested in parallel. The
  decision rests on precedent instead: `client/playwright.config.ts` sets `fullyParallel: true` with

findings.after: In "Blocking from day one", replace the appeal to a no-flake measurement with its real scope: say the sixty-run study covered /play's default loaded state and that the long-score state was byte-identical across fourteen runs; that the remaining nine states (landing, Skeleton, engine error, transport toggles, both popovers, ghost hover, header tooltip, narrow viewport) are unmeasured and two of them cannot be measured until Plan C ships; and that retries: 2 on CI plus the per-shot document.fonts.ready and 500 ms settle are what absorb a one-off blip — the same absorber the parallelism bullet already names.
findings.why_it_works: It keeps the settled day-one blocking decision and removes only the false warrant, replacing it with the mechanism that actually absorbs a blip. A reader then knows which shots carry evidence and which carry a bet.
findings.spike: SPIKED AND CONFIRMED, counts exact: 2 of 11 shots have determinism data, 9 do not, and 2 of those 9 cannot have any because the popovers do not exist yet. The doc's parallelism bullet (:572-580) concedes the gap rather than closing it, and the Risks section offers fullyParallel: false only as a fallback.
findings.verification_reason: The doc warrants day-one blocking on "the measurement found no flake" (:509), but the measurement covers one state in three crop shapes plus a 14-run long-score check - 2 of 11 shots - and the doc itself concedes the measured shots ran at --workers=1 while CI runs parallel.
findings.contradiction_note: The doc's own parallelism bullet (:572-580) concedes the gap rather than closing it, and the Risks section offers `fullyParallel: false` only as a fallback if the difference "bites". Nothing else supplies determinism data for the other nine shots.

findings.section: Readiness, and why each wait is there (301-317, 354-363, 369-371)
findings.title: Both long-score waits carry no timeout, inheriting the 5 s default this section rejects
findings.route: Proposed fix (concrete fix, needs your confirmation)
findings.scenario: The long-score shot starts failing now and then with a bare "expected count 0" and nothing else to go on. Both of its waits quietly inherited Playwright's 5-second default — the very default this section spends two paragraphs saying is too small for /play. The toast lives 4.2 seconds and the measured wait already reaches 4.13 of them, so there is under a second of slack, and that figure came from a one-worker run while CI runs several.
findings.whats_wrong: Neither prescribed long-score wait names a ceiling, while EVERY sibling wait in the same section states one (30 000 / 60 000 / 10 000 ms). Two consequences: the toast-gone assertion has ~871 ms of margin against the toast's measured life; and the data-file assertion — the belt the spec adds for the 15 ms window in which the loading-bar wait can pass early — becomes the parse gate with six times less budget than the lane it was copied from, which gives it { timeout: 30_000 }.

before.text:
**Those three numbers are the existing lane's, and they only work if the per-test budget is
raised with them.** Playwright's `expect` default is 5 000 ms, nowhere near what `/play` needs:
every readiness wait in `web/e2e/a11y.e2e.ts` and `web/e2e/player.e2e.ts` spends 30 000 ms on
the notation `svg`, 60 000 ms on `transport-play` and 10 000 ms on the bar's unmount. But a

findings.title: The element-clip ban rests on evidence taken at a tolerance the doc then rejects
findings.scenario: Later on you want one tightly-cropped shot of a single control, and you read that element-clipped shots are ruled out by measurement. But the measurement behind that rule was taken at zero tolerance, and the drift it found is thousands of times under the tolerance the doc actually adopts two consequences later.
findings.whats_wrong: The three consequences are introduced as "all evidence-backed rather than guessed", yet the element-clip drift was measured at threshold 0 / maxDiffPixels 0, and consequence 3 then adopts a default under which that drift is invisible — and even concedes a stricter setting "would make element-clipped shots impossible", which is an admission that the adopted default permits them.

before.text:
Sixty runs in `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble`, three shots × twenty runs each, at
`threshold: 0` and `maxDiffPixels: 0` — the harshest comparison Playwright allows, where a single
| Notation box only (element-clipped)     | 3 / 19         |

Three design consequences, all evidence-backed rather than guessed:

1. **Page-level shots only** — no `toHaveScreenshot` on a clipped element.
2. **No mask over the notation.** The score is shot as it is drawn.
3. **Playwright's default tolerance is enough** — decided 2026-09-26. Its `threshold` defaults to
   `0.2` in YIQ colour space and `maxDiffPixels` is unset, so a pixel must differ noticeably to
   count and then a _single_ such pixel fails. The worst drift measured here is ±1/255 in one
   channel, about `0.004` — fifty times under that threshold. Going stricter (`threshold: 0`) would
   buy nothing the evidence points at, would make element-clipped shots impossible, and would give
   the repo two comparison policies instead of one. So the shots pass no comparison options at all,
   exactly as `client/` does.

findings.after: Qualify consequence 1: note that the element-clip drift was measured at threshold 0 / maxDiffPixels 0 and sits far inside the default tolerance adopted in consequence 3, so page-level-only is a deliberate choice to keep one shot shape and one comparison policy rather than something the measurement forces.
findings.why_it_works: It keeps the rule while making its real basis legible, so a later author who wants a clipped shot argues with a design choice instead of with evidence that does not actually forbid it.
findings.spike:
SPIKED AND CONFIRMED, and stronger than claimed. The measured element-clip drift scores 0.16 against the 1408.6 cutoff — about 8,800x under in the comparator's own units (~94x in threshold units). The reviewer's "tens of times" was echoing the doc's own conservative "fifty times under" at :105.

UNRAISED BUT ADJACENT: the doc's "about 0.004 — fifty times under that threshold" (:105) is itself inexact; the drift is ~0.0021 in threshold units, so ~94x, not 50x. It sits inside the same range L4-F-1 edits, so it may be worth revisiting in that same pass.
findings.verification_reason: Consequence 1 is derived from drift measured at threshold 0, and at the tolerance the doc actually adopts that same drift produces zero counted pixels, so page-level-only is a consistency choice as claimed - and the doc itself concedes as much at :106.
findings.contradiction_note: The doc contains no other justification for page-level-only; consequence 3 at :105-108 supplies the concession the finding leans on ("would make element-clipped shots impossible") rather than rebutting it.
